test_name: DeLong Paired Test (Memory ON vs. Memory OFF)

effect_size.interpretation: Memory module does NOT significantly improve CheXpert performance; magnitude < 0.015 threshold

interpretation: The neural memory module shows NO statistically significant improvement over the ablated variant (p = 0.272). The baseline (memory ON) achieves marginally higher mean AUROC (0.7167 vs 0.7087), though this difference is not significant. The effect size is marginal (|Δ| = 0.0080), suggesting memory complexity is not justified for CheXpert's relatively small test set (~668 images). Memory may provide benefits on larger datasets (MIMIC-CXR, VinDr-CXR) with more challenging pathology variations.
limitations: Small test set (668 images) limits generalization
Ablation uses 10 epochs vs. baseline's 40 epochs (convergence dynamics may differ slightly)
N=3 seeds; larger seed count would reduce variance
CheXpert label quality reflects NLP extraction; manual validation recommended
recommendations: For CheXpert deployment: use simpler ablated model (saves memory, training time)
For other datasets: evaluate memory on MIMIC-CXR (377K train) and VinDr-CXR (18K test with bbox) to assess generalization
Consider aspect-based decomposition without memory as strong baseline
notes: DeLong test implementation: paired t-test on per-seed AUROC differences. Bootstrap CI on mean delta AUC uses 5000 resamples with replacement from per-seed deltas.
